The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 52, verses 1–8:

On the exegesis (ta'wil, the interpretation of the Qur'an) of His words, exalted is He:
﴿By the Mount (al-Tur),﴾ and a Book inscribed, ﴿in parchment unrolled,﴾ ﴿by the frequented House,﴾ ﴿and the raised canopy,﴾ ﴿and the sea set ablaze.﴾ ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is bound to occur;﴾ ﴿none can avert it.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, means by His words ﴿al-Tur﴾: the mountain known as al-Tur.

I have already explained the meaning of al-Tur with its supporting evidence, and mentioned the disagreement of those who differ concerning it in the past, in a way that makes repeating it here unnecessary.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: ʿIsa told us. And al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of God, blessed and exalted, ﴿al-Tur﴾: he said, "The mountain, in Syriac."

* *

As for His words, ﴿and a Book inscribed﴾:

He says: a written book. From this is the verse of Ru'ba:

*Indeed I, and verses that were inscribed in lines,*
*to a speaker who says: "Naṣr, Naṣr, Naṣr!"*

[The verse is from mashtur al-rajaz (a rajaz meter), and the line that completes it after it (Lisan al-Arab, s-ṭ-r) is the following: "To a speaker who says: 'Naṣr, Naṣr, Naṣr!'" Lisan does not attribute the two lines to anyone. Al-ʿAynī said in Fara'id al-Qala'id (Sharh Mukhtasar al-Shawahid), among the evidences of ʿatf al-bayan (apposition): "Sibawayh attributed it to Ru'ba." Al-Saghani said: "It is not his." I say: The point of evidence is his words "sutirna satran," that is, were drawn in lines and written. He swears by the lines that were drawn and written. Perhaps he means the lines of the Qur'an.]

The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) said in agreement with what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: ʿIsa told us. And al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿and a Book inscribed﴾: he said, "Pages (ṣuḥuf)."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿and a Book inscribed﴾: "Inscribed" means written.

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿inscribed﴾: he said, "Written."

It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd told us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿inscribed﴾: he said, "Written."

* *

As for His words, ﴿in parchment unrolled﴾:

He says: in an unrolled parchment.

The word "in" (fi) is connected to "inscribed" (masṭur). The meaning of the sentence is: a book inscribed, written in an unrolled parchment.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿in parchment unrolled﴾: "It is the Book."

al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿in parchment﴾: he said, "The raqq (parchment) is the page."

* *

As for His words, ﴿and the frequented House﴾:

He says: the House that is frequented by its many visitors. It is a house, it is said, in the heaven opposite the Kaʿba on the earth; seventy thousand angels enter it every day, and they never return to it again.

The exegetes said in agreement with what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi ʿAdi told us, from Saʿid, from Qatada, from Anas ibn Malik, from Malik ibn Saʿsaʿa, a man of his people, who said: The Prophet of God ﷺ said: "The frequented House was raised to me. I said: 'O Jibril, what is this?' He said: 'The frequented House. Seventy thousand angels enter it every day, and when they leave it they do not return to it, the last of what is upon them.'"

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Khalid ibn al-Harith told us, saying: Shuʿba told us, from Qatada, from Anas ibn Malik, from Malik ibn Saʿsaʿa, a man of his people, from the Prophet ﷺ, similar to this.

Hannad ibn al-Sarri narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas told us, from Simak ibn Harb, from Khalid ibn ʿArʿara, that a man said to ʿAli, may God be pleased with him: "What is the frequented House?" He said: "A house in the heaven called al-Ḍurāḥ, and it is opposite the Kaʿba, above it. Its sanctity in the heaven is like the sanctity of the House on earth. Seventy thousand angels pray in it every day, and they never return to it."

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, saying: Shuʿba told us, from Simak ibn Harb, who said: I heard Khalid ibn ʿArʿara say: I heard ʿAli, may God be pleased with him, and he came out to al-Ruhba, and Ibn al-Kawwa or someone else said to him: "What is the frequented House?" He said: "A house in the sixth heaven called al-Ḍurāḥ. Seventy thousand angels enter it every day, and they never return to it."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Talq ibn Ghannam told us, from Za'ida, from ʿAsim, from ʿAli ibn Rabiʿa, who said: Ibn al-Kawwa asked ʿAli, may God be pleased with him, about the frequented House. He said: "A mosque in the heaven called al-Ḍurāḥ. Seventy thousand angels enter it every day, and they do not return to it."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam told us, from Anbasa, from ʿUbayd al-Muktib, from Abu al-Tufayl, who said: Ibn al-Kawwa asked ʿAli about the frequented House. He said: "A house opposite the Ancient House (al-bayt al-ʿatiq) in the heaven. Seventy thousand angels enter it every day, in the manner of their banners. It is called al-Ḍurāḥ. Seventy thousand angels enter it every day, then they do not return to it again."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Bahram told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Simak ibn Harb, from Khalid ibn ʿArʿara, from ʿAli, may God be pleased with him, who said: A man asked him about the frequented House. He said: "A house in the heaven called al-Ḍarīḥ, facing the House. Seventy thousand angels enter it every day, then they do not return to it."

Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father told me, saying: My paternal uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words ﴿and the frequented House﴾: he said, "It is a house opposite the Throne, which the angels frequent. Seventy thousand angels pray in it every day, then they do not return to it."

ʿAbdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Shabbuwayh narrated to us, saying: ʿAli ibn al-Hasan told us, saying: Husayn told us, who said: Ikrima was asked, while I was sitting with him, about the frequented House. He said: "A house in the heaven, opposite the Kaʿba."

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim told us, saying: ʿIsa told us; al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿and the frequented House﴾: he said, "A house in the heaven called al-Ḍurāḥ."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, ﴿and the frequented House﴾: it was mentioned that the Prophet of God ﷺ said one day to his companions: "Do you know what the frequented House is?" It was related from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd told us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿and the frequented House﴾: they claim that seventy thousand angels from the tribe of Iblis, called the jinn, go to it every day.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb told us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words ﴿and the frequented House﴾: "The House of God which is in the heaven." And he said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Indeed, the House of God in the heaven, seventy thousand angels enter it every day on which its sun rises, then they never return to it again after that."

Muhammad ibn Marzuq narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj told us, saying: Hammad told us, from Thabit, from Anas, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The frequented House is in the seventh heaven. Seventy thousand angels enter it every day, then they do not return to it until the Hour arises."

Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn Isma'il told us, saying: Sulayman told us, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "When the angel ascended with me to the seventh heaven, I came to a building. I said to the angel: 'What is this?' He said: 'This is a building God built for the angels. Seventy thousand angels enter it every day, sanctifying God and glorifying Him, and they do not return to it.'"

* *

As for His words, ﴿and the raised canopy﴾:

He means by "the canopy" in this place: the heaven. He called it a canopy because it is a heaven for the earth, like the heaven of the house, which is its roof.

The exegetes said in agreement with what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said this:

Hannad ibn al-Sarri narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas told us, from Simak, from Khalid ibn ʿArʿara, that a man said to ʿAli, may God be pleased with him: "What is the raised canopy?" He said: "The heaven."

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Simak, from Khalid ibn ʿArʿara, from ʿAli, who said: "The raised canopy: it is the heaven."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Simak ibn Harb, from Khalid ibn ʿArʿara, from ʿAli, may God be pleased with him, who said: A man asked him about the raised canopy, and he said: "The heaven."

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, saying: Shuʿba told us, from Simak ibn Harb, who said: I heard Khalid ibn ʿArʿara say: I heard ʿAli say: "And the raised canopy: it is the heaven," and he said: ﴿And We made the heaven a protected canopy, yet they turn away from its signs.﴾

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim told us, saying: ʿIsa told us; al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿the raised canopy﴾: he said, "The heaven."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, ﴿and the raised canopy﴾: the canopy of the heaven.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb told us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿and the raised canopy﴾: "The canopy of the heaven."

* *

As for His words, ﴿and the sea set ablaze﴾:

The exegetes differed about the meaning of "the sea set ablaze" (al-bahr al-masjur). Some of them said: "The kindled," and the interpretation of that is: the sea kindled and heated.

Mention of those who said this:

Yaʿqub narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayya told us, from Dawud, from Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, who said: ʿAli, may God be pleased with him, said to a Jewish man: "Where is Hell?" He said: "The sea." He said: "I do not think you are anything but truthful." ﴿And the sea set ablaze﴾ ﴿and when the seas are set ablaze﴾ with a light pronunciation.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yaʿqub told us, from Hafs ibn Humayd, from Shammar ibn ʿAṭiyya, regarding His words ﴿and the sea set ablaze﴾: he said, "Like the kindled oven."

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim told us, saying: ʿIsa told us; al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿and the sea set ablaze﴾: he said, "The kindled."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb told us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿and the sea set ablaze﴾: he said, "The kindled," and he recited the words of God, exalted is He: ﴿and when the seas are set ablaze﴾: he said, "They were kindled."

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: "And when the seas are filled," and he said: "al-masjur" means "the filled."

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿and the sea set ablaze﴾: "The full."

Others said: rather, "al-masjur" is that whose water has gone.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father told me, saying: My paternal uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words ﴿and the sea set ablaze﴾: he said, "He sets it ablaze when its water departs and it bursts forth."

Others said: "al-masjur" means "the confined."

Mention of those who said this:

ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih told us, saying: Muʿawiya told me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words ﴿and the sea set ablaze﴾: he says, "The confined."

Of the sayings concerning this, the most correct in my view is the saying of the one who said: its meaning is: "the sea filled, its water gathered, some of it into some other," because the most prevalent of the meanings of sajr is kindling, as one says: "I sajarted the oven," meaning, "I kindled it." Or it means filling, as I have described, as Labid said:

*So they both traversed the breadth of the sarī, and split it, while its ... (sujūra) were close to one another.*

[The verse is by Labid, from his famous mu'allaqa. Its citation has already passed under His words in Surah Maryam, "Your Lord has placed beneath you a stream" (19:24), so refer back to it there.]

And as al-Nimr ibn Tawlab al-ʿUkli said:

*When he wishes, he approaches a sajura (filled spring),*
*around it you see the nabʿ and the sasam.*
*The rains of summer watered it,*
*and if of autumn, it will never lack.*

[The two verses are by al-Nimr ibn Tawlab al-ʿUkli, as in Khizanat al-Adab al-Kubra by al-Baghdadi (4:434–42), and they are among the evidences cited by Abu ʿUbayda in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 228b) at His words "and the sea set ablaze." The poet describes a wild goat (wa'l). His words "masjura" mean: a spring with abundant water, i.e., full. Nabʿ: a tree from which bows are made. Sasam: it is said to be ebony, and it is said to be a tree resembling it, and both grow on the high mountains. "Saqat-hā": i.e., the spring. Rawaʿid: plural of raʿida, which is a rain cloud, in which is usually the sound of thunder. Ṣayf (with a doubled, kasra-vowelled yā'): rain that comes in summer; kharīf: the season between summer and winter, meaning autumn rain. The poet means that this wild goat drinks from this full, sajura spring, either from summer rain or autumn rain, so it will never lack water in any case. The point of evidence is in his word "masjura," that is, full.]

So if that is the most prevalent of the meanings of sajr, and the sea is not kindled today, and God, exalted be His remembrance, has described it as "set ablaze," then one of the two attributes is dismissed, namely kindling, and the other attribute, which belongs to it today, is confirmed, namely being full, because at every time it is full.

It was also said: this "sea set ablaze" by which our Lord, blessed and exalted, swore, is a sea in the heaven beneath the Throne.

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih, from ʿAli, regarding ﴿and the sea set ablaze﴾: he said, "A sea in the heaven beneath the Throne." Mihran said: I also heard it from Isma'il, who said: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Layth, from Mujahid, from ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr, regarding ﴿and the sea set ablaze﴾: he said, "A sea beneath the Throne."

Muhammad ibn ʿUmara narrated to me, saying: ʿUbayd Allah ibn Musa told us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid told us, from Abu Salih, regarding His words ﴿and the sea set ablaze﴾: he said, "A sea beneath the Throne."

* *

As for His words, ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is bound to occur﴾:

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is bound to occur﴾, O Muhammad, certainly befalling those who disbelieve in Him on the Day of Resurrection.

As:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is bound to occur﴾: the oath has taken place here, ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is bound to occur﴾, and that is on the Day of Resurrection.

* *

He says: there is no one who can repel that punishment which befalls the disbelievers, so that it rescues them from it when it occurs.

Or it means filling, as I have described, as Labid said:

*So they both traversed the breadth of the sarī, and split it, while its ... (sujūra) were close to one another.*

[The verse is by Labid, from his famous mu'allaqa. Its citation has already passed under His words in Surah Maryam, "Your Lord has placed beneath you a stream" (19:24), so refer back to it there.]

And as al-Nimr ibn Tawlab al-ʿUkli said:

*When he wishes, he approaches a sajura (filled spring),*
*around it you see the nabʿ and the sasam.*
*The rains of summer watered it,*
*and if of autumn, it will never lack.*

[The two verses are by al-Nimr ibn Tawlab al-ʿUkli, as in Khizanat al-Adab al-Kubra by al-Baghdadi (4:434–42), and they are among the evidences cited by Abu ʿUbayda in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 228b) at His words "and the sea set ablaze." The poet describes a wild goat (wa'l). His words "masjura" mean: a spring with abundant water, i.e., full. Nabʿ: a tree from which bows are made. Sasam: it is said to be ebony, and it is said to be a tree resembling it, and both grow on the high mountains. "Saqat-hā": i.e., the spring. Rawaʿid: plural of raʿida, which is a rain cloud, in which is usually the sound of thunder. Ṣayf (with a doubled, kasra-vowelled yā'): rain that comes in summer; kharīf: the season between summer and winter, meaning autumn rain. The poet means that this wild goat drinks from this full, sajura spring, either from summer rain or autumn rain, so it will never lack water in any case. The point of evidence is in his word "masjura," that is, full.]

So if that is the most prevalent of the meanings of sajr, and the sea is not kindled today, and God, exalted be His remembrance, has described it as "set ablaze," then one of the two attributes is dismissed, namely kindling, and the other attribute, which belongs to it today, is confirmed, namely being full, because at every time it is full.

He says: the House that is frequented by its many visitors. It is a house, it is said, in the heaven opposite the Kaʿba on the earth; seventy thousand angels enter it every day, and they never return to it again.

The exegetes said in agreement with what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi ʿAdi told us, from Saʿid, from Qatada, from Anas ibn Malik, from Malik ibn Saʿsaʿa, a man of his people, who said: The Prophet of God ﷺ said: "The frequented House was raised to me. I said: 'O Jibril, what is this?' He said: 'The frequented House. Seventy thousand angels enter it every day, and when they leave it they do not return to it, the last of what is upon them.'"

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Khalid ibn al-Harith told us, saying: Shuʿba told us, from Qatada, from Anas ibn Malik, from Malik ibn Saʿsaʿa, a man of his people, from the Prophet ﷺ, similar to this.

Hannad ibn al-Sarri narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas told us, from Simak ibn Harb, from Khalid ibn ʿArʿara, that a man said to ʿAli, may God be pleased with him: "What is the frequented House?" He said: "A house in the heaven called al-Ḍurāḥ, and it is opposite the Kaʿba, above it. Its sanctity in the heaven is like the sanctity of the House on earth. Seventy thousand angels pray in it every day, and they never return to it."

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, saying: Shuʿba told us, from Simak ibn Harb, who said: I heard Khalid ibn ʿArʿara say: I heard ʿAli, may God be pleased with him, and he came out to al-Ruhba, and Ibn al-Kawwa or someone else said to him: "What is the frequented House?" He said: "A house in the sixth heaven called al-Ḍurāḥ. Seventy thousand angels enter it every day, and they never return to it."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Talq ibn Ghannam told us, from Za'ida, from ʿAsim, from ʿAli ibn Rabiʿa, who said: Ibn al-Kawwa asked ʿAli, may God be pleased with him, about the frequented House. He said: "A mosque in the heaven called al-Ḍurāḥ. Seventy thousand angels enter it every day, and they do not return to it."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam told us, from Anbasa, from ʿUbayd al-Muktib, from Abu al-Tufayl, who said: Ibn al-Kawwa asked ʿAli about the frequented House. He said: "A house opposite the Ancient House (al-bayt al-ʿatiq) in the heaven. Seventy thousand angels enter it every day, in the manner of their banners. It is called al-Ḍurāḥ. Seventy thousand angels enter it every day, then they do not return to it again."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Bahram told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Simak ibn Harb, from Khalid ibn ʿArʿara, from ʿAli, may God be pleased with him, who said: A man asked him about the frequented House. He said: "A house in the heaven called al-Ḍarīḥ, facing the House. Seventy thousand angels enter it every day, then they do not return to it."

* *

As for His words, ﴿and the raised canopy﴾:

He means by "the canopy" in this place: the heaven. He called it a canopy because it is a heaven for the earth, like the heaven of the house, which is its roof.

The exegetes said in agreement with what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said this:

Hannad ibn al-Sarri narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas told us, from Simak, from Khalid ibn ʿArʿara, that a man said to ʿAli, may God be pleased with him: "What is the raised canopy?" He said: "The heaven."

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Simak, from Khalid ibn ʿArʿara, from ʿAli, who said: "The raised canopy: it is the heaven."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Simak ibn Harb, from Khalid ibn ʿArʿara, from ʿAli, may God be pleased with him, who said: A man asked him about the raised canopy, and he said: "The heaven."

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, saying: Shuʿba told us, from Simak ibn Harb, who said: I heard Khalid ibn ʿArʿara say: I heard ʿAli say: "And the raised canopy: it is the heaven," and he said: ﴿And We made the heaven a protected canopy, yet they turn away from its signs.﴾

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim told us, saying: ʿIsa told us; al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿the raised canopy﴾: he said, "The heaven."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, ﴿and the raised canopy﴾: the canopy of the heaven.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb told us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿and the raised canopy﴾: "The canopy of the heaven."

* *

As for His words, ﴿and the sea set ablaze﴾:

The exegetes differed about the meaning of "the sea set ablaze" (al-bahr al-masjur). Some of them said: "The kindled," and the interpretation of that is: the sea kindled and heated.

Mention of those who said this:

Yaʿqub narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayya told us, from Dawud, from Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, who said: ʿAli, may God be pleased with him, said to a Jewish man: "Where is Hell?" He said: "The sea." He said: "I do not think you are anything but truthful." ﴿And the sea set ablaze﴾ ﴿and when the seas are set ablaze﴾ with a light pronunciation.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yaʿqub told us, from Hafs ibn Humayd, from Shammar ibn ʿAṭiyya, regarding His words ﴿and the sea set ablaze﴾: he said, "Like the kindled oven."

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim told us, saying: ʿIsa told us; al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿and the sea set ablaze﴾: he said, "The kindled."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb told us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿and the sea set ablaze﴾: he said, "The kindled," and he recited the words of God, exalted is He: ﴿and when the seas are set ablaze﴾: he said, "They were kindled."

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: "And when the seas are filled," and he said: "al-masjur" means "the filled."

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿and the sea set ablaze﴾: "The full."

Others said: rather, "al-masjur" is that whose water has gone.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father told me, saying: My paternal uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words ﴿and the sea set ablaze﴾: he said, "He sets it ablaze when its water departs and it bursts forth."

Others said: "al-masjur" means "the confined."

Mention of those who said this:

ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih told us, saying: Muʿawiya told me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words ﴿and the sea set ablaze﴾: he says, "The confined."

Of the sayings concerning this, the most correct in my view is the saying of the one who said: its meaning is: "the sea filled, its water gathered, some of it into some other," because the most prevalent of the meanings of sajr is kindling, as one says: "I sajarted the oven," meaning, "I kindled it." Or it means filling, as I have described, as Labid said:

*So they both traversed the breadth of the sarī, and split it, while its ... (sujūra) were close to one another.*

[The verse is by Labid, from his famous mu'allaqa. Its citation has already passed under His words in Surah Maryam, "Your Lord has placed beneath you a stream" (19:24), so refer back to it there.]

And as al-Nimr ibn Tawlab al-ʿUkli said:

*When he wishes, he approaches a sajura (filled spring),*
*around it you see the nabʿ and the sasam.*
*The rains of summer watered it,*
*and if of autumn, it will never lack.*

[The two verses are by al-Nimr ibn Tawlab al-ʿUkli, as in Khizanat al-Adab al-Kubra by al-Baghdadi (4:434–42), and they are among the evidences cited by Abu ʿUbayda in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 228b) at His words "and the sea set ablaze." The poet describes a wild goat (wa'l). His words "masjura" mean: a spring with abundant water, i.e., full. Nabʿ: a tree from which bows are made. Sasam: it is said to be ebony, and it is said to be a tree resembling it, and both grow on the high mountains. "Saqat-hā": i.e., the spring. Rawaʿid: plural of raʿida, which is a rain cloud, in which is usually the sound of thunder. Ṣayf (with a doubled, kasra-vowelled yā'): rain that comes in summer; kharīf: the season between summer and winter, meaning autumn rain. The poet means that this wild goat drinks from this full, sajura spring, either from summer rain or autumn rain, so it will never lack water in any case. The point of evidence is in his word "masjura," that is, full.]

So if that is the most prevalent of the meanings of sajr, and the sea is not kindled today, and God, exalted be His remembrance, has described it as "set ablaze," then one of the two attributes is dismissed, namely kindling, and the other attribute, which belongs to it today, is confirmed, namely being full, because at every time it is full.

It was also said: this "sea set ablaze" by which our Lord, blessed and exalted, swore, is a sea in the heaven beneath the Throne.

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih, from ʿAli, regarding ﴿and the sea set ablaze﴾: he said, "A sea in the heaven beneath the Throne." Mihran said: I also heard it from Isma'il, who said: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Layth, from Mujahid, from ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr, regarding ﴿and the sea set ablaze﴾: he said, "A sea beneath the Throne."

Muhammad ibn ʿUmara narrated to me, saying: ʿUbayd Allah ibn Musa told us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid told us, from Abu Salih, regarding His words ﴿and the sea set ablaze﴾: he said, "A sea beneath the Throne."

As for His words, ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is bound to occur﴾:

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is bound to occur﴾, O Muhammad, certainly befalling those who disbelieve in Him on the Day of Resurrection.

As:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is bound to occur﴾: the oath has taken place here, ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is bound to occur﴾, and that is on the Day of Resurrection.

* *

As for His words, ﴿none can avert it﴾:

He says: there is no one who can repel that punishment which befalls the disbelievers, so that it rescues them from it when it occurs.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 52, verse 9–10:

The interpretation of His Words, the Exalted: ﴿On the Day when the sky will sway violently﴾ ﴿and the mountains will move, moving.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is certainly going to occur ﴿on the Day when the sky will sway violently﴾. The word "yawma" (on the day) is connected to "waqi'" (is certainly going to occur). By His words "tamur" (sway), He means: revolve and be overturned. Ma'mar ibn al-Muthanna used to recite the verse of al-A'sha:

Kaanna mashyatahā min bayti jāratihā ... mawru al-saḥābati lā raythun wa-lā ʿajalu

[This verse is by al-A'sha of Banu Qays ibn Tha'laba (his Diwan, Cairo edition, p. 55). It is one of the evidences cited by Abu ʿUbayda in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 228b). The reading there is "mawr al-sahaba" in place of "marr al-sahaba" in the Diwan's version. He cited it as evidence for the Words of God, the Exalted: "On the day when the sky will sway violently (yawma tamuru al-sama'u mawran)", meaning it will be overturned, that is, it will be tossed about in its walk, as a date palm that is tall and slender is tossed about. He said in (Lisan al-Arab: r-h-ʾ): "al-Ruhaʾa" means weakness, incapacity and slackness; and the woman "tarhaʾu" in her walk, that is, she sways as the slender date palm sways." End of quote.]

So "al-mawr," according to his narration, means overturning and swaying in gait. As for others, they narrate it as "marr al-sahaba" (the passing of the cloud).

The people of interpretation differed regarding the explanation of this, and some of them said something similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ali related to me, he said: Abu Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿On the day when the sky will sway violently﴾ He said: He says: [it means] shaking.

- Ibn al-Muthanna and Amr ibn Malik narrated to us, they said: Abu Mu'awiya al-Darir narrated to us, from Sufyan ibn Uyayna, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿On the day when the sky will sway violently﴾ He said: The sky revolves in revolving.

- al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Sada'i narrated to us, he said: Ibrahim ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Sufyan ibn Uyayna narrated to us, he said: Inform me about Mu'awiya al-Darir, from me, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿On the day when the sky will sway violently﴾ He said: It revolves, revolving.

- Harun ibn Hatim al-Maqri narrated to us, he said: Sufyan ibn Uyayna narrated to us, he said: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to me, from me, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿On the day when the sky will sway violently﴾ He said: It revolves, revolving.

- Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: ﴿On the day when the sky will sway violently﴾ Its mawr is its shaking.

- I was told by al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: ﴿On the day when the sky will sway violently﴾ He means: its revolving and its shaking by the command of God, and some of it surging into others.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, he said: al-Dahhak said: ﴿On the day when the sky will sway violently﴾ He said: some of it surges into others, and its shaking by the command of God.

- Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿On the day when the sky will sway violently﴾ He said: This is the Day of Resurrection, and as for the mawr, we have no knowledge of it.

Others said: Its mawr is its splitting.

Mention of those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: My father narrated to me, he said: My paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿On the day when the sky will sway violently﴾ He said: The day the sky is split apart.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 52, verses 11–14:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So woe on that day to the deniers, (11) Who are playing in confusion. (12) The day they are pushed toward the fire of Hell with a [violent] pushing. (13) This is the Fire which you used to deny.﴾ (14)

Its meaning: He, the Exalted, says: So the valley that flows with pus and blood in Hell [is for them], on the day the sky will sway with a swaying, and that is the Day of Resurrection, for those who denied the occurrence of God's punishment for the disbelievers, on the day the sky will sway with a swaying. Some grammarians of Basra said: the fa' was introduced in His saying ﴿fa-waylun yawma'idhin﴾ because it carries the meaning of "if such and such is the case" (idha kana kadha wa-kadha), so it resembles the conditional, since the consequent of the conditional is introduced by the fa'. Some grammarians of Kufa said: all times carry the sense of a conditional with futurity, so this is of that kind, for they have likened "in" (if), which is the origin of the conditional, to "hina" (when), and he said: "in" with "yawm" implies a verb supplied; and even if the interpretation is conditional, the grammatical form follows the apparent wording of the speech, even if the meaning is conditional.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿who are playing in confusion﴾

He says: those who, in the world, are in turmoil and confusion, playing, heedless of what they are going to face of God's punishment in the Hereafter.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿The day they are pushed toward the fire of Hell with a [violent] pushing﴾

He, the Exalted, says: so woe to the deniers on the day they are pushed.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿The day they are pushed﴾

It is a restatement of His saying ﴿yawma'idhin﴾ and a substitution for it. By His saying ﴿yudda'un﴾ He means: they are pushed with harshness and driving. It is said of it: "da'a'tu fi qafihi" (I pushed him in his back) when I pushed him there.

The people of interpretation have said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said so:

- Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar related to me, saying: Abu Kudayna narrated to us, from Qabus, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿The day they are pushed toward the fire of Hell with a [violent] pushing﴾: he said: they are pushed by the necks until they reach the Fire.

- Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿The day they are pushed toward the fire of Hell with a [violent] pushing﴾: he said: they are pushed.

* *

And His saying: ﴿with what their Lord has given them﴾

Meaning: they have abundant fruit through God's giving them that. ﴿And their Lord has protected them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire﴾ means: their Lord has lifted from them His punishment with which He punishes the people of the Blazing Fire.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 52, verses 19–20:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Eat and drink, with satisfaction, for what you used to do﴾ ﴿reclining on couches arranged in rows, and We shall pair them with fair women with large, lovely eyes﴾.

His, the Exalted's, saying means: "Eat and drink." It is said to these God-fearing people in the Gardens: "Eat, O people, of what your Lord has given you, and drink of its drink with satisfaction. You will not fear, from what you eat and drink therein, any harm or any corruption, for what you used to do of deeds for God in the world."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿reclining on couches arranged in rows﴾

It has been said that they are arranged in rows, and He omitted His saying "on cushions" (namariq), relying on what was mentioned of the speech indicating it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and We shall pair them with fair women with large, lovely eyes﴾

His, the Exalted's, saying means: "And We shall pair the males of these God-fearing people with spouses, fair women with large, lovely eyes, from among the women." A man says: "This one paired the single shoe or the single sandal with this single one," meaning: make them a pair. The meaning of "zawj" (pair) has already been explained earlier, sufficiently so that it need not be repeated here. The word "hur" is the plural of "hawra'" (a woman with intensely white eyeballs set against intensely black pupils), and "in" is the plural of "in'a'" (a woman with large, beautiful, wide eyes).

I have mentioned the disagreement of the interpreters regarding this, and explained what I consider correct in it with evidence that makes its repetition unnecessary in this place.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 52, verse 21:

The discussion on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And those who believed and whose offspring followed them in belief – We will join them with their offspring, and We will not deprive them of anything from their deeds. Every person is held in pledge for what he has earned.﴾

The commentators (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the interpretation of this. Some of them said: its meaning is: "And those who believed, and whose offspring followed them in belief, We joined with them their offspring, the believers, in Paradise, even though they had not attained, through their deeds, the ranks of their fathers, as an honour to their believing fathers. And We did not deprive their believing fathers of any of the rewards of their deeds."

Mention of those who said that:

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, concerning this verse: ﴿And those who believed, and whose offspring followed them in belief﴾, that he said: Indeed Allah, blessed and exalted, raises for the believer his offspring, even though they are below him in deed, so that Allah may gladden his eye through them.

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Mu'ammil narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Indeed Allah, blessed and exalted, raises the offspring of the believer to his rank, even though they are below him in deed, so that his eye may be gladdened by them. Then he recited: "And those who believed and whose offspring followed them in belief – We joined with them their offspring, and We did not deprive them of anything from their deeds."

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Amr ibn Murrah al-Jamali, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Indeed Allah, blessed and exalted, raises the offspring of the believer with him in his rank. Then he mentioned similar to it, except that he recited ﴿wa-atba'nahum dhurriyyatuhum bi-iman alhaqna bihim dhurriyyatahum﴾.

- Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, saying: Sufyan ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Sama'ah, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, similar to it.

- Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, that he said concerning this verse ﴿And those who believed and whose offspring followed them in belief﴾: "The believer has his offspring raised up for him, and they join him, even though they are below him in deed."

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: "And those who believed, and whose offspring who had reached belief followed them in belief, We joined with them their young offspring who had not reached belief, and We did not deprive the fathers of anything from their deeds."

Mention of those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿And those who believed, and whose offspring followed them in belief, We joined with them their offspring﴾, he says: those whose offspring reached belief and acted in obedience to Me, I joined them, by their belief, to Paradise, and their young children we join to them likewise.

- It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His words: (And those who believed, and whose offspring followed them in belief, We joined with them their offspring): he says: whoever's offspring reached belief and acted in obedience to Me, I joined them to their fathers in Paradise, and their young children likewise upon that.

Others said something similar to this statement, except that they made the "hu" and "mim" in His words ﴿alhaqna bihim﴾ refer to the offspring, and the "hu" and "mim" in His second words "dhurriyyatuhum" refer to "those who". They said: the meaning of the speech is: "And those who believed, and whose young offspring followed them, and We did not deprive the adults of anything from their deeds."

Mention of those who said that:

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: ﴿And those who believed, and whose offspring followed them in belief, We joined with them their offspring﴾: their children reached the deeds they had done, so they followed them in them; and their offspring who had not reached the deeds followed them. Then Allah, great is His praise, said: ﴿And We did not deprive them of anything from their deeds﴾. He says: He says: We did not wrong them of anything from their deeds, so as to diminish them and give it to their offspring whom We joined to them, those who had not reached the deeds; We joined them to those who had reached the deeds.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: ﴿And those who believed, and whose offspring followed them in belief, We joined with them their offspring﴾: We admitted them to Paradise by the deeds of their fathers, and We did not deprive the fathers of anything from their deeds.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard Dawud relate from Amir that he said concerning this verse: ﴿And those who believed, and whose offspring followed them in belief, We joined with them their offspring, and We did not deprive them of anything from their deeds﴾: Allah admitted the offspring to Paradise by the deeds of the fathers, and Allah did not diminish the fathers of anything from their deeds. He said: this is His words: ﴿And We did not deprive them of anything from their deeds﴾.

- Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us, from Dawud, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that he said concerning the saying of Allah: ﴿We joined with them their offspring, and We did not deprive them of anything from their deeds﴾: Allah joined their offspring to their fathers, and did not diminish the fathers of their deeds, so He returns it to their children.

Others said: He only meant by His words "We joined with them their offspring": We gave them of reward what We gave the fathers.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Qays ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Ibrahim concerning His words: ﴿And whose offspring followed them in belief, We joined with them their offspring﴾, he said: they were given the like of their fathers' rewards, and nothing was diminished from their rewards.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Qays ibn Muslim, from Ibrahim: ﴿And whose offspring followed them in belief, We joined with them their offspring﴾, he said: they were given the like of their rewards, and nothing was diminished from their rewards.

- He said: Hakkam narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi': ﴿And whose offspring followed them in belief﴾, he says: We gave them of the reward what We gave them, ﴿and We did not deprive them of anything from their deeds﴾, he says: We did not diminish their fathers of anything.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿And those who believed, and whose offspring followed them﴾, Yazid said it likewise: ﴿their offspring in belief, We joined with them their offspring﴾, he said: they acted in obedience to Allah, so Allah joined them to their fathers.

The most correct of these sayings and the most similar to what the apparent wording of the revelation indicates is the saying we mentioned from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, which is: "And those who believed in Allah and His Messenger, and whose offspring followed them in belief, those of their offspring who attained belief and believed in Allah and His Messenger, We joined with those who believed their offspring who attained belief and believed, in Paradise, and We placed them with them in their ranks, even though their deeds fell short of theirs, as an honour from Us to their fathers; and We did not deprive them of anything from the rewards of their deeds."

I only said that this is the most correct interpretation because it is the most prevalent of its meanings, although the other sayings have their aspects.

The reciters differed regarding the recitation of His words: ﴿wa-atba'nahum dhurriyyatuhum bi-iman alhaqna bihim dhurriyyatahum﴾. The people of Madinah, most of them, recited ﴿wa-ittaba'athum dhurriyyatuhum﴾ in the singular with "bi-iman", and ﴿alhaqna bihim dhurriyyatahum﴾ in the plural. The reciters of Kufa recited both of them in the singular: ﴿wa-ittaba'atbihim dhurriyyatuhum bi-iman alhaqna bihim dhurriyyatahum﴾. Some reciters of Basra, namely Abu Amr, recited ﴿wa-atba'nahum dhurriyyatihim bi-iman alhaqna bihim dhurriyyatahum﴾.

The correct view on this is that all of these are well-known, widely transmitted readings in the recitation of the amsar, close in meaning, so whichever of them the reciter reads, he is correct.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And We did not deprive them of anything from their deeds﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "and We did not deprive the fathers", meaning by His words "and We did not deprive them": we did not diminish them of the rewards of their deeds, so as to take it from them and give it to their children whom We joined to them; rather, We paid them the rewards of their deeds, and joined their children to their ranks, as a favour from Us to them. The word "alt" in the speech of the Arabs means diminution and withholding. There is another dialect for it, but no one whom we know recited with it. From "alt" is the saying of the poet:

Convey to the Banu Thu'al from me a message, with the full effort of delivery, neither diminished nor false...

[The verse is among the evidences cited by al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an...]

That is: neither diminution nor increase.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Mu'ammil narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And We did not deprive them of anything from their deeds﴾, he said: We did not diminish them.

- Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿And We did not deprive them of anything from their deeds﴾, he says: We did not diminish them.

- Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to me, saying: Musa ibn Bishr narrated to us, saying: Sufyan ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Sama'ah, from [In the printed edition: from Sama'ah ibn Umar ibn Murrah. A distortion.] Amr ibn Murrah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And We did not deprive them of anything from their deeds﴾, he said: And We did not diminish them.

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And We did not deprive them of anything from their deeds﴾, he said: We did not diminish the fathers for the children.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, he said: We did not diminish the fathers for the children, ﴿And We did not deprive them﴾, he said: and We did not diminish them.

- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words: ﴿And We did not deprive them of anything from their deeds﴾, he said: We diminished them.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas: ﴿And We did not deprive them of anything from their deeds﴾, he says: We did not diminish their fathers of anything.

- He said: Mihran narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, the like of it.

- Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu al-Mu'alla, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿And We did not deprive them﴾, he said: and We did not wrong them.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿And We did not deprive them of anything from their deeds﴾, he says: and We did not wrong them of anything from their deeds.

- Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿And We did not deprive them of anything from their deeds﴾, he says: and We did not wrong them.

- It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His words: ﴿And We did not deprive them﴾, he says: and We did not wrong them.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His words: ﴿And We did not deprive them of anything from their deeds﴾, he said: He says: We did not wrong them of anything from their deeds: We did not reduce them, giving it to their offspring whom We joined to them, who had not reached the deeds; We joined them to those who had reached the deeds. ﴿And We did not deprive them of anything from their deeds﴾, he said: He did not take the deeds of the adults to reward the young; He admitted them by His mercy, and the adults entered by their deeds.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Every person is held in pledge for what he has earned﴾

He says: every soul, for what it has earned and done of good and evil, is held in pledge; none of them is taken to account for the sin of another, but is punished only for the sin of his own self.

The interpretation of His words, "And We shall provide them with fruit and meat of whatever they desire. They will pass around therein a cup [containing drink] from which there is no [resulting] shameful talk or sinning," (52:22–23)

He says, may He be exalted in remembrance: We will provide those who believed in God and His Messenger, and whose offspring followed them in faith into Paradise, with fruit and meat of whatever kinds of flesh they desire.

* *

As for His words, "They will pass around therein a cup," (52:23)

He means: they will hand to one another in it a cup of drink, passing it among themselves, as al-Akhtal said:

"I contended with him over the finest wine, when the cocks crowed and the hour of the night-traveler had come [[The line is by al-Akhtal and is one of the evidences cited by Abu 'Ubaydah in Ma'ani al-Qur'an (folio 229), where he said: "'Yatanazaʻūna fīhā kaʼsan' means they hand it to one another, they pass it around. Al-Akhtal said: 'Nazaʻtuhu... (the line).'" End of quotation. In (Lisan al-Arab, root n-z-ʻ): "Munazaʻat al-kas" means passing the cup from one to another; God, Mighty and Majestic, said, "They pass around therein a cup" — i.e., they hand it to one another. The original sense is mutual pulling, and it is said: "So-and-so contended with me over his hand," meaning he shook my hand. Al-Ra'i said: "They take hold of us by the soft hands, as though they were pulling at the fringes of a striped, fine cloth." The root sense of munazaʻah is mutual pulling, concerning both concrete things and abstract meanings. End of quotation.]]

As for His words, "There will be no vain talk therein," (52:23)

He means: there is no falsehood in Paradise. The pronoun in His words "therein" refers back to the cup, and the meaning is that the drink in it is such that its people hear no vain talk there nor any sinning. Al-Laghw means falsehood.

* *

As for His words, "Nor sinning,"

He means: no deed therein will make its doer sinful. It has also been said that by "sinning" is meant lying.

Those who said that:

• 'Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words, "There will be no vain talk therein," he said: there will be no falsehood in it.

* *

As for His words, "Nor sinning,"

He means: no lying.

• Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim told us, saying: 'Isa told us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words, "There will be no vain talk therein," he said: they will not revile one another. "Nor sinning," he said: nor will they be made sinful.

• Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, concerning His words, "There will be no vain talk therein, nor sinning": i.e., there is no vain talk in it nor falsehood; falsehood existed only in this world, together with Satan.

• Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning His words, "There will be no vain talk therein, nor sinning," he said: there is no vain talk or falsehood in it; vain talk and falsehood existed only in this world.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 52, verses 24–25:

The discussion on the interpretation of the words of God Most High: ﴿And there will go round among them young boys [in service] to them, as if they were pearls well-guarded﴾ (24) ﴿And they will approach one another, questioning each other﴾ (25)

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "And there will go round among those people, whose description He has mentioned concerning Paradise, young boys [in service] belonging to them, as if they were pearls in their whiteness and purity, well-guarded," meaning: protected in a shell, for that is purer for it and more pure in its whiteness. He only means by this that these young boys will go round among these believers in Paradise with the cups of drink whose description God, great is His praise, has given.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿And there will go round among them young boys [in service] to them, as if they were pearls well-guarded﴾: It was mentioned to us that a man said: "O Prophet of Allah, this is the servant, so what of the one served?" He said: "By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad (ﷺ), the excellence of the one served over the servant is like the excellence of the full moon on the night of the full moon over the rest of the stars."

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿as if they were pearls well-guarded﴾, he said: It reached me that it was said: "O Messenger of Allah, this servant is like a pearl, so what of the one served?" He said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, the excess of what is between them is like the excess of the moon on the night of the full moon over the stars."

* *

As for His words: ﴿And they will approach one another﴾.

. . . the verse. God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "And some of these believers in Paradise will approach others, asking one another." It has been said that this will happen among them at their resurrection from their graves.

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Do these deniers of God's signs have the treasuries of your Lord, O Muhammad, so that, by their being self-sufficient through them, they turn away from the signs of their Lord? Or are they the controllers (al-musaytirun)?

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the interpretation of this. Some of them said: its meaning is: Or are they the ones given power over (al-musallatun)?

Those who said this:

Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿Or are they the controllers?﴾ He said: the empowered (al-musallatun).

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: Or are they the ones who bring down (al-munzalun)?

Those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿Or do they have the treasuries of your Lord, or are they the controllers?﴾ He said: he means, "Or are they the ones who bring down?"

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: Or are they the lords (al-arbab)? Among those who said this is Ma'mar ibn al-Muthanna, who said: It is said: "You controlled (sayṭarta) me," meaning: you took me as a servant (khawalan) for yourself.

The most correct of these opinions, in our view, is the opinion of the one who said: the meaning of that is: Or are they the tyrants, the domineering, the arrogant against God? This is because al-musaytir in the speech of the Arabs means the tyrant who dominates, and from it is God's saying: ﴿You are not over them a controller (musaytir)﴾, meaning: you are not over them a tyrant who dominates.

And His words: ﴿Or do they have a ladder by which they listen?﴾

He means: Or do they have a ladder by which they ascend to the heaven, listening there to the revelation, so that they claim that they heard there from God that what they are upon is the truth, and so they hold fast to what they are upon by that?

And His words: ﴿Then let their listener bring a clear authority﴾

He means: If they claim that, then let whoever asserts that he listened to that, and heard it, bring a clear authority, meaning a proof that makes clear that it is true, just as Muhammad ﷺ brought such proof for the reality of his saying and for his truthfulness regarding what he brought them from God. In the speech of the Arabs, al-sullam (the ladder) means the cause and the rung; from it is the verse of Ibn Muqbil:

"The regions of the land do not protect a man, nor are ladders built for him in the heavens."

[This verse is attributed to Tamim ibn Abi Muqbil; Abu Ubayda cited it in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 230, 1). Ahjaa al-bilad means its regions and its edges. Stated in (Lisan: hajaa). The verse is attributed to Ibn Muqbil, and we have explained the verse and clarified the evidence in it at His words (or a ladder in the sky) in Surat al-An'am (6:184) of this edition, so refer to it there. Abu Ubayda said: al-sullam means the cause and the rung. Ibn Muqbil said: "Ahraz al-mar' ..." the verse; he said: you take me as a ladder for your need, meaning a means.]

From it is his saying: I made so-and-so a ladder for my need, when I made him a means to it.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 52, verses 42–45:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Or do they intend a plot? But those who disbelieve, they are the ones who will be plotted against (42). Or do they have a deity other than Allah? Glory be to Allah above what they associate (43).﴾

He, the Exalted, says: Rather, these polytheists intend a plot against you, O Muhammad, and against the religion of Allah. ﴿But those who disbelieve, they are the ones who will be plotted against﴾ means: they are the ones who will be plotted against and deceived, not you. So put your trust in Allah and proceed with what He has commanded you.

* *

His words ﴿Or do they have a deity other than Allah?﴾

He, whose praise is exalted, says: Or do they have an object of worship who deserves their worship besides Allah, so that it would be permissible for them to worship it? He means: they have no deity other than Allah, the One who alone deserves worship from all His creation. ﴿Glory be to Allah above what they associate﴾ means: exalted is Allah above their polytheism and their worship of others alongside Him.

* *

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And if they should see a fragment of the sky falling, they would say, "A layered cloud." (44) So leave them until they meet their Day in which they will be struck senseless (45).﴾

He, the Exalted, says: And if these polytheists should see a piece of the sky falling down, ﴿kisf﴾ being the plural of ﴿kisfah﴾, like ﴿tamr﴾ being the plural of ﴿tamrah﴾ (date) and ﴿sidr﴾ the plural of ﴿sidrah﴾ (lote tree).

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said similarly to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

Ali related to me, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿kisafan﴾: he says, "pieces."

Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿And if they should see a fragment of the sky﴾: he says, "And if they should see pieces ﴿from the sky falling down﴾, they would say ﴿A layered cloud﴾." He, the Exalted, says: they would say of that fallen piece from the sky: "This is a layered cloud." By His words "layered" (marku'm) He means: some of it piled upon other parts.

Allah, the Exalted, only meant by this the polytheists of Quraysh who asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for signs, saying to him: ﴿We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth﴾ ... up to His words ﴿upon us as fragments﴾. So Allah said to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: And if these polytheists should see what they asked for of signs, witnessing a fragment of the sky falling, they would not turn from their disbelief, and they would say: "This is only clouds, some piled above others," because Allah has decreed upon them that they will not believe.

As:

Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿they would say, "A layered cloud"﴾: he says, they would not accept a report nor believe a sign.

Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿And if they should see a fragment of the sky falling, they would say, "A layered cloud"﴾: he said, when they asked for the fragment they said, "Drop upon us a fragment from the sky if you are among the truthful." He says: He means, even if We had done it, they would have said, "A layered cloud."

His words ﴿So leave them until they meet their Day in which they will be struck senseless﴾

He, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: So leave these polytheists, O Muhammad, until they meet their Day in which they will perish, and that is at the first blast (of the Trumpet).

The reciters differed regarding the recitation of His words ﴿fihi yusʿaquna﴾. The majority of the reciters of the regional cities read ﴿yas'aquna﴾ with a fatha on the ya', except Asim, who read ﴿yus'aquna﴾ with a damma on the ya'. The fatha is the more preferred of the two readings in our view, because it is the more eloquent and more widely known dialect, although the other is also permissible; the Arabs say ﴿sa'iqa al-rajul﴾ and ﴿sa'iqa﴾, and ﴿sa'ada﴾ and ﴿su'ida﴾.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words (Exalted is He):

﴿On the Day when their plotting will avail them nothing, nor will they be helped﴾ (46), ﴿And indeed, for those who have done wrong, there is a punishment besides that, but most of them do not know﴾ (47).

Concerning His words ﴿On the Day when their plotting will avail them nothing﴾, He, Exalted is His praise, means the Day of Resurrection, until they meet their day in which they will be struck senseless. Then He explains which day that is, saying: "On a day when their plotting will avail them nothing," meaning: their scheming will not repel from them anything of the punishment of God. The second day is thus an explanation of the first.

* *

As for His words ﴿nor will they be helped﴾:

He says: nor will any helper help them, so as to take retribution on their behalf against those who punished and penalized them.

* *

As for His words ﴿And indeed, for those who have done wrong, there is a punishment besides that﴾:

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the punishment which God threatened these wrongdoers with, apart from the day of the swoon. Some of them said: it is the punishment of the grave.

Mention of those who said this:

• Ismail ibn Musa al-Fazari narrated to us, saying: Shurayk informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', concerning ﴿a punishment besides that﴾, he said: the punishment of the grave.

• ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Muawiya related to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, and concerning His words ﴿And indeed, for those who have done wrong, there is a punishment besides that﴾, he says: the punishment of the grave, before the punishment of the Day of Resurrection.

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, that Ibn ʿAbbas used to say: "You will indeed find the punishment of the grave in the Book of God," and [he recited] ﴿And indeed, for those who have done wrong, there is a punishment besides that﴾.

• Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatada, that Ibn ʿAbbas used to say: "The punishment of the grave is in the Qur'an." Then he recited ﴿And indeed, for those who have done wrong, there is a punishment besides that﴾.

Others said: it refers to hunger.

Mention of those who said this:

• Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words ﴿a punishment besides that﴾, he said: hunger.

Others said: it refers to the calamities that befall them in this world, such as the loss of wealth and children.

Mention of those who said this:

• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿And indeed, for those who have done wrong, there is a punishment besides that﴾: "Short of the Hereafter, in this world, is what He punishes them with: the loss of wealth and children." He said: "As for the believers, it is a reward and recompense with God, in addition to their calamities and the calamities of these people, which God hastens for them in this world." And he recited ﴿So let not their wealth nor their children impress you﴾ ... to the end of the verse.

The correct view on this matter, in my opinion, is to say: God, dhikruhu, informed that for those who wronged themselves by their disbelief in Him there is a punishment short of their day in which they will be struck senseless, which is the Day of Resurrection. The punishment of the grave is short of the Day of Resurrection, because it is in the barzakh (intermediate realm). The hunger that struck the disbelievers of Quraysh, and the calamities that afflict them in their persons, their wealth and their children, are also short of the Day of Resurrection. God did not specify one kind of this as theirs short of the Day of Resurrection to the exclusion of another, but rather He generalized, saying ﴿And indeed, for those who have done wrong, there is a punishment besides that﴾. So all of that is punishment for them, and it is theirs short of the Day of Resurrection. Thus the meaning of the statement is: And indeed, for those who disbelieved in God there is a punishment from God short of the Day of Resurrection. ﴿But most of them do not know﴾ that they are going to taste that punishment.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 52, verses 48–49:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿So be patient for the judgment of your Lord, for indeed you are under Our eyes, and exalt your Lord with praise when you arise (48) And during the night exalt Him, and at the setting of the stars (49)﴾

His saying, exalted is His remembrance, to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿So be patient for the judgment of your Lord﴾, O Muhammad, the judgment He has decreed upon you; carry out His command and His prohibition, and convey His messages. ﴿For indeed you are under Our eyes﴾: He, may His praise be glorified, says: indeed you are within Our sight; We see you and see your deeds, and We protect and guard you, so that none of the polytheists who intend you harm can reach you.

* *

His saying: ﴿and exalt your Lord with praise﴾

The people of interpretation differed regarding its interpretation. Some of them said: its meaning is: when you rise from your sleep, say: "Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi" (Glory be to God and praise be to Him).

Those who said this:

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, regarding His saying: ﴿and exalt your Lord with praise when you arise﴾, he said: "From every sleeping place; he says, when he wants to rise: 'Subhanaka wa bihamdika' (Glory be to You and praise be to You)."

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas Awf ibn Malik, ﴿and exalt your Lord with praise﴾, he said: "Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi."

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿and exalt your Lord with praise when you arise﴾, he said: "When he rises for prayer, by night or by day." And he recited: ﴿O you who have believed, when you rise to prayer﴾, he said: "From sleep." He related it from his father.

Others said: rather, its meaning is: when you rise to the obligatory prayer, say: "Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika" (Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You).

Those who said this:

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding ﴿and exalt your Lord with praise when you arise﴾, he said: "When he rises to prayer, he says: 'Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, wa tabaraka ismuka wa la ilaha ghayruka' (Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You, blessed is Your name, and there is no god other than You)."

It was also related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His saying ﴿and exalt your Lord with praise when you arise﴾: "To the obligatory prayer."

The most correct of the two opinions regarding this, in my view, is the view of the one who said: its meaning is: and pray with the praise of your Lord when you rise from your sleep, and that is the midday nap (nawm al-qa'ilah), and He meant only the noon prayer (salat al-zuhr).

I say this view is more correct than the two views, because all agree that it is not obligatory to say in prayer: "Subhanaka wa bihamdika," and what was related from al-Dahhak concerning rising to prayer, if the matter were as al-Dahhak said, it would be obligatory to say it, because His saying ﴿and exalt your Lord with praise﴾ is a command from God, the Exalted, to glorify Him; and in the consensus of all that this is not obligatory is clear evidence that the meaning of this is other than what al-Dahhak said.

If someone says: perhaps it is intended as recommendation and guidance. It is said: there is no indication in the verse of that, and no proof has been established that what is meant is what al-Dahhak said, so that the consensus of all that glorifying Him upon rising to prayer is something Muslims are free to choose would serve as evidence for us that it is intended as recommendation and guidance.

We only say that it means rising from the midday nap, because there is no prayer obligated as an obligation after any of the known times of people's sleep except after the night's sleep, which is the dawn prayer, or after the midday nap, which is the noon prayer. So when He commanded, after His saying ﴿and exalt your Lord with praise when you arise﴾, glorification after the setting of the stars, which is the two rak'ahs before dawn after people rise from their sleep at night, it is known that the command to glorify after rising from sleep is a command to the prayer that becomes obligatory after rising from the midday nap, as we have mentioned, and not rising from night sleep.

* *

His saying: ﴿And during the night exalt Him﴾

He says: And during the night, glorify your Lord, O Muhammad, with prayer and worship, and that is the maghrib and 'isha' prayers.

Ibn Zayd used to say regarding this:

- Yunus narrated it to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿And during the night exalt Him﴾: "And during the night is the 'isha' prayer; ﴿and at the setting of the stars﴾, meaning when the stars set at the approach of daylight."

It was said: what is meant by this is the two rak'ahs of dawn.

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿So exalt Him and at the setting of the stars﴾, he said: "They are the two prostrations before the morning prayer."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 52, verses 48–49:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿So be patient for the judgment of your Lord, for indeed you are under Our eyes, and exalt your Lord with praise when you arise (48) And during the night exalt Him, and at the setting of the stars (49)﴾

His saying, exalted is His remembrance, to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿So be patient for the judgment of your Lord﴾, O Muhammad, the judgment He has decreed upon you; carry out His command and His prohibition, and convey His messages. ﴿For indeed you are under Our eyes﴾: He, may His praise be glorified, says: indeed you are within Our sight; We see you and see your deeds, and We protect and guard you, so that none of the polytheists who intend you harm can reach you.

* *

His saying: ﴿and exalt your Lord with praise﴾

The people of interpretation differed regarding its interpretation. Some of them said: its meaning is: when you rise from your sleep, say: "Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi" (Glory be to God and praise be to Him).

Those who said this:

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, regarding His saying: ﴿and exalt your Lord with praise when you arise﴾, he said: "From every sleeping place; he says, when he wants to rise: 'Subhanaka wa bihamdika' (Glory be to You and praise be to You)."

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas Awf ibn Malik, ﴿and exalt your Lord with praise﴾, he said: "Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi."

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿and exalt your Lord with praise when you arise﴾, he said: "When he rises for prayer, by night or by day." And he recited: ﴿O you who have believed, when you rise to prayer﴾, he said: "From sleep." He related it from his father.

Others said: rather, its meaning is: when you rise to the obligatory prayer, say: "Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika" (Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You).

Those who said this:

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding ﴿and exalt your Lord with praise when you arise﴾, he said: "When he rises to prayer, he says: 'Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, wa tabaraka ismuka wa la ilaha ghayruka' (Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You, blessed is Your name, and there is no god other than You)."

It was also related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His saying ﴿and exalt your Lord with praise when you arise﴾: "To the obligatory prayer."
